answer: We define a protocol where nodes commit dynamic opportunity-cost bonds to a slashing matrix that triggers subgame-perfect penalties if identities deviate from verifiable zero-knowledge proofs. As an adversary attempts to wander across sub-networks to forge Sybil identities, the cumulative capital barrier functions like a dry dune shifting against an unyielding river of protocol enforcement. Expected attack utility remains strictly negative because the marginal cost of staked collateral exceeds the diluted reward share, ensuring a Nash equilibrium where honest node behavior persists.
